subject: Renewal: EU primary residency + staged APAC rollout / failover ops
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@junctionhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@junctionhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:18:00Z
Subject: Renewal + EU residency + APAC rollout — draft ask

Jordan — thanks for taking this. We're up for renewal and want to lock in a path that meets two needs: (1) EU primary data residency (we need EU-only for patient data at rest) and (2) an APAC staged rollout for peak hours (burst capacity + warm standby for disaster failover).

High level asks:
- 12 month renewal starting Jul 1 with EU primary tenancy and a documented APAC warm-standby plan.
- SLA for cross-region failover < 5min for control-plane failover, and best-effort for in-flight sessions.
- Clear pricing uplift for APAC burst capacity and for on-call support during cutovers.
- SOC2 evidence and a brief ops runbook for our security review.

I've attached a short requirements spreadsheet and a sample redline from our legal team. Can your team propose pricing and a staged delivery timeline? We need procurement-friendly language for the contract.

Thanks,
Liam

Subject: Re: Renewal + EU residency + APAC rollout — draft ask

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet. We can do EU primary residency and a staged APAC rollout with explicit warm standby and failover play. I've looped in Marissa (commercial) and Soojin (ops) to scope the delivery and pricing.

Preliminary approach:
- Renewal term: 12 months (Jul 1 start).
- Residency: EU primary (data at rest in EU region + contract amendment to residency clause).
- APAC: staged rollout in two waves — (1) APAC burst (capacity on-demand) for peak hours; (2) warm-standby node configured for cross-region failover.
- Failover SLA: we can commit to an operational runbook targeting ~5min RTO for control-plane re-routing; in-flight model sessions will be best-effort and depend on session affinity settings.

Action items for us:
1) Marissa — draft commercial terms (delta pricing for APAC burst + residency amendment, plus optional 24/7 on-call).
2) Soojin — ops to draft failover runbook and proposed cutover windows (canaries, production smoke tests).
3) Legal — we'll propose a short contract addendum for the residency clause and failover responsibilities.

I'll pull together a revised SOW and share a DocuSign link for signatures once we agree on pricing.

Jordan

Team — rough numbers and timeline below (for discussion with Liam). This is an internal note — I'll convert to customer-facing pricing text once we agree.

Commercial delta (monthly, USD):
- Base renewal (current usage profile): $48,000/mo.
- EU residency add-on (data at rest + geo-fencing): +$4,500/mo (one-time data migration assistance fee: $18k).
- APAC burst capacity (reserve for peak 0800-1200 SGT): +$6,000/mo for reserved burst units; pay-as-you-go beyond reserved.
- Warm-standby (hot nodes ready for failover): +$3,000/mo (includes 2x warm replicas and readiness tests).
- 24/7 on-call during cutover (optional, per-weekend block): $1,800/block.

Timeline (target start Jul 1):
- May 7-14: legal redlines; finalize SOW.
- May 15-31: ops design and prep (APAC topology, DNS play).
- Jun 7-14: dry-run canary in non-prod + runbook validation.
- Jun 21-25: production canary and final smoke tests.
- Jul 1: go-live (EU residency active; APAC staged in warm-standby).

Attachments I'm preparing: SOW_JunctionHealth_V2.pdf (includes language for residency amendment), SOC2-report-summary.pdf (ops evidence). Expect those by EOD.

Thanks Marissa — high level looks reasonable. A few procurement questions before we proceed:
1) Can you confirm whether EU residency add-on requires any downtime during the cutover? If so, what windows?
2) For the warm-standby nodes — are they billed for storage charges in APAC while idle? We need cost predictability.
3) For the failover SLA and in-flight session behavior, legal wants explicit language that outlines responsibilities and acceptable RTOs.

Also sending a soft redline from our legal team (attached). If we can get the SOW and the short addendum today, procurement will expedite review.

Liam

Subject: Re: Renewal + EU residency + APAC rollout — draft ask

Liam — answers below and next steps.

1) Downtime during EU cutover: planned data migration requires a short maintenance window for write-locking user-managed buckets (target 30–90 minutes during off-hours). We'll coordinate exact UTC windows with you; suggested window: Sun Jun 20 02:00–05:00 UTC.

2) Warm-standby billing: warm nodes will incur compute and storage reservation fees (we've captured these as the warm-standby line item). We can provide a sweet-spot reservation that minimizes idle storage charges; any additional egress or long-term snapshot storage will be billed separately and capped per the SOW.

3) Failover SLA language (proposal): Redwood will maintain operational procedures and routines to initiate cross-region routing to APAC warm-standby within 5 minutes of qualified control-plane failure. In-flight model sessions: best-effort; we will provide a configurable session-affinity TTL. Detailed responsibilities and escalation flows are included in the ops addendum.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: finalize SOW and produce a short residency + failover addendum.
- Soojin: attach the ops runbook and schedule the dry-run for Jun 7–14.
- Legal: we'll append the proposed SLA text and upload DocuSign.

I'm uploading the SOW and runbook to the shared drive and preparing a DocuSign envelope: https://redwood.app/docusign/JHC-2027-RNW-42

If procurement is happy, we'll aim to sign by Mon May 17.

Jordan
